items.title: Rauf says people interests come first in Melaka political cooperation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the interests of the state and its people would take precedence in any political cooperation. Earlier, Rauf announced that the Melaka state assembly would be dissolved tomorrow. Rauf, who is BN chairman, said the BN Plus approach provided room for all parties to engage in discussions, but any decision would be based on BN's interests and strength in the state.

items.title: 11 hurt as teen opens fire outside Turkiye school
items.summary: TURGUTLU: A teenager opened fire outside a high school in western Turkiye on Tuesday, wounding 11 people before being detained by police, a minister said. School shootings are rare in Turkiye, although there were two attacks in April on consecutive days in southern Turkiye that sparked widespread anger. - SCHOOL SAFETY - The attack came five months after two back-to-back school shootings that raised public concerns about security in Turkish schools.

items.title: Van driver fined RM12,000 for abusing two stepchildren with pestle, iron
items.summary: Sessions Court judge Suhaila Haron fined Joharis Mahmod, 48, RM12,000 for two counts of abusing the boys aged 17 and 9. She ordered Joharis to serve five months in jail if he fails to pay the fine. Investigations found that Joharis had slapped the younger child's cheeks five times and beaten the older child with a pestle and an iron.

items.title: BigBang KL concert tickets snapped up in under 5 minutes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tickets for BigBang's Kuala Lumpur concert sold out in less than 5 minutes during the general sale today, leaving thousands of fans scrambling for seats to the highly anticipated show. He said the individual approached him through his Threads post after he indicated that he was looking for tickets to the concert. She said the service helped her secure 2 tickets during the V.I.P.

items.title: [UPDATED] Negri Sembilan MB suspends two top state officials
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan government has suspended state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal with immediate effect, Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said today. In a statement, Ismail said the decision was made unanimously at a special meeting of the state executive council (MMKN) today. He said state financial officer Datuk Masri Razali would perform the duties of state secretary until a new state secretary is appointed by the Chief Secretary to the Government.

items.title: URTI, asthma, conjunctivitis cases decline amid persistent haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Upper respiratory tract infections (URTI), asthma and conjunctivitis cases have declined, but the Health Ministry has urged the public to continue taking precautions as the haze persists. The ministry said the haze affecting several parts of the country had entered its seventh week, while surveillance at 78 designated health facilities nationwide showed a decline in all three haze-related illnesses in epidemiological week (ME) 37/2026 compared with ME 36/2026. URTI, asthma and conjunctivitis cases are also monitored daily through the 78 designated health facilities and assessing air quality readings alongside health surveillance data to determine appropriate public health measures.

items.title: Singapore online safety commission receives over 500 reports in first two months
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Online Safety Commission (OSC) received more than 500 reports of online harm in its first two months of operation, resolving over 90 per cent of eligible cases. "The bulk of them are doxxing and online harassment, with a far smaller proportion involving intimate image abuse and online stalking," she said on the "Let's Table It" podcast aired on the gov.sg YouTube channel on Tuesday. According to OSC data, doxxing accounted for the largest share of reports at 44 per cent, followed by online harassment (38 per cent), intimate image abuse (eight per cent), online stalking (seven per cent) and image-based child abuse (three per cent).

items.title: Scheduled water disruption in Seremban, Rembau, PD until Thursday
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Consumers in parts of Seremban, Rembau and Port Dickson will experience a scheduled water supply disruption from today until Thursday due to maintenance works at the Sungai Terip and Sawah Raja water treatment plants (WTPs). Syarikat Air Negri Sembilan Sdn Bhd (SAINS), in a Facebook post today, said the affected areas in Seremban include Senawang, Rasah, Rahang, Ampangan, Seremban 2 and Sikamat. In Rembau, the disruption affects Kampung Kundur Hilir, Taman Akasia Kundur, Exevalley Orchard Park, Pengkalan Durian, Kampung Sungai Radin, Kampung Sungai Timun Dalam and Kampung Sungai Timun Luar.

items.title: BHESS, EC start engagement on increasing Sabah and Sarawak parliamentary seats
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah and Sarawak Affairs Division (BHESS) of the Prime Minister's Department has initiated engagement with the Election Commission (EC) to discuss the direction and implementation mechanism for the proposal to increase the number of members of parliament (MPs) from Sabah and Sarawak. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said he led BHESS on a courtesy call to EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun today to discuss the matter. Mustapha said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had also expressed that there was justification for increasing the ratio of MPs from Sabah and Sarawak, subject to further discussions with EC.

items.title: MQA calls for structured drone training at higher education institutions
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA) chief executive officer Datuk Prof Mohamad Shatar Sabran has called for structured drone operation training to be organised by higher education institutions. "Drone operation has been identified as a high-impact emerging skill that warrants formal training recognition, in line with the shift in the country's higher education landscape towards alternative learning pathways through micro-credential programmes," he said in a statement today. He said the Higher Education Ministry is now encouraging all local higher education institutions to roll out specialised skills-based programmes such as drone operation more aggressively.

items.title: Man jailed 10 years, six strokes over sexual offences against teenage girlfriend
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A man who checked into a motel twice with his teenage girlfriend was sentenced to 10 years in jail and six strokes of the rotan for raping and sexually assaulting the girl. On the first charge, Mohd Ashriff was sentenced to nine years in jail and two strokes of the rotan for raping the girl, who was then 15 years and seven months old, in a motel room in Sipitang on Jan 23. He was sentenced to 10 years in jail and two strokes of the rotan on the second charge of raping the same girl at the same motel on March 24.

items.title: Student opens fire outside school in Turkiye, eight pupils wounded, NTV reports
items.summary: ANKARA: A student opened fire in front of their high school in Turkiye's western province of Manisa on Tuesday, wounding at least eight other pupils, broadcaster NTV reported. Two of the wounded were in a critical condition, NTV said. The assailant was caught, the local governor's office said.

items.title: Indonesia's rainy season delayed to November as El Nino persists
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia is expected to experience a shorter than usual rainy season this year starting in November, the weather agency said on Tuesday, with the El Nino weather pattern to last until the first quarter of 2027. The agency previously forecast it would come in October, when the wet season usually starts. About 61 per cent of Indonesia's land area will experience the delayed rainy season, agency chief Teuku Faisal Fathani told a press conference.

items.title: Tasik Bera enforcement: Five arrested, investigation papers to be referred to DPP
items.summary: Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the reports were lodged by members of the Orang Asli community and enforcement personnel. Azry Akmar said the investigation papers on five individuals arrested on Sept 15 for allegedly obstructing enforcement officers during the operation would be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor soon. In an unrelated development, Azry Akmar said police had opened two investigation papers following a recent altercation at a religious school in Bukit Ibam, Rompin.

items.title: Rauf: Thank you, Melaka people
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh today thanked the people of the state as the legislative assembly is set to be dissolved tomorrow. "Thank you to the people of Melaka. We (the state executive councillors) have worked together for the people.

items.title: Philippine bus operators press Marcos for fare hike as fuel costs soar
items.summary: MANILA: Philippine bus operators pressed President Ferdinand Marcos on Tuesday to let them raise ticket prices, arguing that soaring fuel costs from the Middle East war threatened to make operations "impossible." The Philippine transport board approved a fare hike in March, only for Marcos to quash the move a day later. Ticket prices have remained static ever since.

items.title: Companies must rethink global footprints in light of heightened geopolitical risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Geopolitical risks are prompting companies to rethink their global footprints and strengthen localisation in key markets, as businesses seek greater control over supply chains, costs and market access, veteran corporate leader Tan Sri Abdul Wahid Omar said. Wahid, who is also the non-executive chairman of IOI Corp Bhd, said companies should focus less on the geopolitical event itself and more on how it affects customers, supply chains, cost structures, market access, capital allocation and long-term competitiveness. He said companies must distinguish between temporary market volatility and structural changes that could affect their competitiveness and future valuations.

items.title: PKR’s Hassan Karim urges Anwar to retain Anthony Loke ahead of major transport projects
items.summary: PASIR GUDANG, Sept 22 — Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim has called on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to persuade Anthony Loke to remain as transport minister to ensure the completion of several key infrastructure projects, including those in Johor. The PKR lawmaker expressed concern that Loke’s resignation could jeopardise ongoing projects, including those in Johor. “I hope the prime minister takes my view into consideration and persuades Loke to stay.

items.title: Melaka heads to 16th state election as state assembly dissolved
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: After Johor and Negri Sembilan, Melaka will hold its 16th state election soon following the dissolution of the state assembly which will take effect tomorrow. The Melaka state assembly has 28 seats, with the current state government's mandate scheduled to end on Dec 27. In the 15th Melaka state election held on Nov 20, 2021, Barisan Nasional (BN) formed the state government after winning 21 of the 28 seats, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won five seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.

items.title: Three actors questioned over viral video allegedly mocking Rukun Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have recorded statements from three actors involved in a theatre performance to assist investigations into a viral video allegedly mocking the principles of the Rukun Negara. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said the three, comprising two women and a man aged between 28 and 47, were detained in Selangor and Johor last Saturday. Kumar said preliminary investigations found that five actors were involved in the performance, with statements recorded from three of them.

items.title: MCMC not decision-maker in Na'im Brundage TikTok accounts blocking, High Court rules
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today allowed a preliminary objection by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and four others against Bersatu Youth leader Na'im Brundage's application for leave to initiate judicial review over the blocking of his two TikTok accounts. Judge Norliza Othman, in allowing the objection, said the leave application was premised on the assumption that MCMC (3rd respondent) had directed TikTok to block Na'im's accounts, which could not form the basis for judicial review. Na'im filed the judicial review application on June 24, 2024, naming MCMC chief network security officer Datuk Dr Mohamed Sulaiman Sultan Suhaibuddeen, the MCMC chairman, MCMC, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and the Government of Malaysia as respondents.

items.title: S'gor Bersatu Youth chief fails to initiate judicial review against MCMC, Fahmi
items.summary: Judge Norliza Othman found that the decision to block the accounts had been taken by TikTok and not by MCMC. In her judgment, Norliza said MCMC had made no decision that could be subject to judicial review, as the action to block or suspend the accounts was taken by TikTok. "MCMC only took administrative action by informing TikTok about compliance issues involving the platform's guidelines, while the subsequent action was TikTok's decision.

items.title: Court of Appeal sets Jan 7 next year to deliver decision on Malaysian Bar's Najib pardon appeal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has set Jan 7 next year to deliver its decision on the appeal by the Malaysian Bar who is seeking leave to commence a judicial review to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board's (FTPB) decision to reduce former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's prison sentence and fine in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case. The Malaysian Bar is appealing the Nov 2024 High Court's dismissal of its application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings to quash the Pardons Board's decision. It is also seeking a declaration that the Pardons Board's decision to reduce Najib's fine from RM210 million to RM50 million is similarly illegal, unconstitutional and void.

items.title: Teens as young as 13 caught producing, selling animated CSAM - Cops
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Some of the eight minors detained in a nationwide operation targeting child sexual abuse material (CSAM) were found to have produced and sold animated child sexual abuse material online. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M Kumar said the material was sold to online communities with similar interests, with some pieces reportedly priced at between RM50 and RM60. Kumar said the communities were formed online, with members not necessarily knowing one another personally.

items.title: Thai national among two arrested for misappropriating petrol
items.summary: "During the raid, we found that petrol was being transferred from a locally registered Proton Waja into a Toyota Hilux bearing a Thai registration number," she said in a statement today. She said further inspection of the Proton Waja found that its rear fuel tank had been modified, while the Toyota Hilux was also found to have a modified fuel tank underneath the vehicle. Rohaida said enforcement action was taken under Section 21 of the Control of Supplies Act 1961.

items.title: Seven religious school students arrested over two bullying cases in Rompin
items.summary: KUANTAN: Police have arrested seven religious school students in Rompin over their alleged involvement in two separate bullying incidents this month. The victims were three 14-year-old students studying and residing at the school hostel. Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the first incident, on Sept 12, involved two victims, with police arresting five suspects comprising Form Four and Form Five students aged 16 and 17.

items.title: Rauf vows Melaka public services to continue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The dissolution of the Melaka assembly will not disrupt the administration or essential public services, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said. He said the government would continue to carry out its duties as a caretaker government until a new administration is formed after the election. "The administration, public services, welfare of the people, security and daily government operations will continue as usual.

items.title: More than 2.1 million CSAM, porn files uncovered since 2024
items.summary: The number of arrests under Op Pedo has also increased significantly over the past three years. He said the police and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) integrated Op Pedo 1.0 in 2024 resulted in 13 arrests, before the figure rose to 31 under Op Pedo 2.0 last year. The number of items seized also increased from 37 in Op Pedo 1.0 to 82 in Op Pedo 2.0 and 95 in the latest operation.

items.title: Migrants turn to sea routes to sneak into Kelantan
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Illegal migrants entering Kelantan are now more frequently using sea routes from Tak Bai, Thailand, rather than the Sungai Golok border, Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said. Many are coming through routes from Tak Bai and using the Kelantan River. Yusoff said police had also shared information with the Thai authorities on groups identified as being active in the Tak Bai area for further action.

items.title: OGX Group ventures into renewable energy, targets data centre market
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: OGX Group Bhd has ventured into the renewable energy (RE) industry, targeting opportunities in Malaysia's growing data centre market through battery energy storage systems (BESS). In a statement today, the information technology infrastructure solutions provider said its wholly owned subsidiary OGX Green Tech Sdn Bhd will spearhead the new business. The group said Zhejiang Hyxi Technology Co Ltd (Hyxi), a China-based energy storage and inverter specialist with a presence across Europe, has appointed OGX Green Tech as an authorised distributor to market, distribute and sell Hyxi's products in Malaysia.

items.title: As parents age, Malaysia must plan for neurodivergent adults too, says Nancy Shukri
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Planning for neurodivergent individuals must extend beyond childhood intervention to cover their needs throughout their lifespan, particularly as their parents and caregivers grow older. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said this was increasingly important as neurodivergent individuals were living longer and Malaysia was rapidly transitioning towards an ageing society, with those aged 60 and above expected to make up 15 per cent of the population by 2036. She said disability planning had traditionally focused on early intervention and childhood development, but this needed to be expanded to address the long-term needs of neurodivergent individuals and ageing caregivers.

items.title: Kelantan residents prepare for Super El Nino, fear wells could run dry
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Residents relying on underground water have begun making early preparations for the Super El Nino phenomenon, which is expected to affect the state from November. Most said they were worried that their underground wells, typically 20 to 40 feet deep, could dry up during prolonged hot weather. Grocery shopkeeper Abdul Aziz Wahab, 40, said residents were looking for ways to prevent water shortages.

items.title: Johor man says he collected recyclables to sell, not trouble neighbours
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: "I was collecting the items to sell, not to trouble my neighbours," said a physically disabled elderly man after authorities cleared about 13 tonnes of recyclable materials from his home in Taman Permas Jaya. A photo showed rubbish and recyclable materials piled along the front gate, covering much of the pavement and spilling towards the roadside. "I collect the items to sell.

items.title: Malaysia’s research has potential, now it needs to leave the lab, says higher education minister
items.summary: Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the milestone demonstrated Malaysia’s immense capacity for innovation, provided the gap between academic research and commercial market demands could be bridged effectively. “Malaysia had many good researchers, ideas and promising innovations, but too many of them remained at the university level. “For the first time, we are creating a dedicated platform for university researchers to bring their ideas directly to industry, investors and potential partners,” he said during the opening ceremony of the University Research and Innovation Investment Summit 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here today.

items.title: No drug arrests for a week? Kelantan police chief says two station heads get reprimand letters
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 22 — Two police station chiefs (OCSs) in Kelantan have received reprimand letters after they failed to record any drug-related arrests for a week, said state police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat. He said the state police headquarters is monitoring seven police stations with regard to enforcement against drug abuse and trafficking. Mohd Yusoff said the performance of each police station is monitored weekly and presented at meetings with the head of the Narcotics Department.

items.title: Finance pros cannot escape geopolitics in a changing world, says deputy finance minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Finance professionals must adapt to a rapidly changing global landscape shaped by geopolitical shifts, climate and sustainability challenges, artificial intelligence (AI) and growing concerns over trust. Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the transformation of the global environment in recent years had created new challenges for businesses and finance professionals, requiring them to rethink how financial systems and structures are designed. As such, he emphasised the need for financial professionals to understand geopolitical developments worldwide, particularly as businesses face growing risks to investment, technology and supply chains.

items.title: Melaka heads for polls as CM Rauf Yusoh confirms assembly set for dissolution tomorrow
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 22 — The Melaka State Legislative Assembly will be dissolved tomorrow to pave the way for the 16th state election. Ab Rauf said State Assembly Speaker Datuk Ibrahim Durum had also submitted the notice of dissolution to the Election Commission (EC). They were former Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Idris Haron (BN-Sungai Udang), Datuk Nor Azman Hassan (BN-Pantai Kundor), Datuk Noor Effandi Ahmad (Bersatu-Telok Mas) and independent Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee (Pengkalan Batu).

items.title: Three actors out on bail as police hunt uploader of viral Rukun Negara clip from 2018
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Bukit Aman have released three local actors on police bail after questioning them over a viral video of a 2018 theatre performance allegedly mocking the Rukun Negara, while investigators hunt for the person who re-uploaded the footage. “The three have since been released on police bail after their statements were recorded, and checks found no content from the performance on their mobile phones or other devices. The performing arts centre has since closed, Kumar said.

items.title: From ‘Made in Malaysia’ to ‘Made by Malaysia’: Govt wants R&D to turn more research into commercial gains
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The government is looking to strengthen Malaysia’s research and development (R&D) ecosystem through more market-driven funding mechanisms and closer industry collaboration, said Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. He said Malaysia is shifting from a “Made in Malaysia” to a “Made by Malaysia” approach as it seeks to strengthen value creation and drive economic upgrading, with R&D playing a central role. While Malaysia’s R&D spending has reached about one per cent of gross domestic product, or nearly RM20 billion, he said the main challenge is turning research into commercial results.

items.title: After retiring as police No 2, Ayob Khan takes on new role as UTeM board chairman
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 22 — Former Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay has been appointed chairman of the Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) Board of Directors for a three-year term effective Sept 16. The university said Ayob Khan’s extensive experience in leadership and senior management in one of the country’s key departments was expected to strengthen the UTeM Board’s role in steering the university’s strategic direction sustainably. “UTeM believes his extensive experience and strong strategic management credentials will enable him to lead the UTeM Board in addressing the challenges ahead,” it said.

items.title: Piranha in Pahang? Fisheries Department calls in Aquaria KLCC for DNA backup
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 22 — The Department of Fisheries Malaysia (DOF) will collaborate with Aquaria KLCC to identify fish suspected to be piranhas at Klau Dam, Raub, Pahang, using DNA or environmental DNA (eDNA) analysis. Director-General of Fisheries Datuk Adnan Hussain said the collaboration would leverage live piranha specimens and existing DNA data held by Aquaria KLCC to determine the fish’s identity. Adnan said the Pahang Fisheries Department had instructed inland fishermen at Klau Dam to retain and surrender any fish resembling piranhas for examination of their morphology, scales and teeth.

items.title: Zahid: Neither MB Ismail Lasim nor I was summoned by Negeri Sembilan Ruler for an audience
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said neither he nor Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was summoned for an audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Negeri Sembilan here yesterday. Neither the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar nor I was ever summoned for an audience. The institutions and establishment in Negeri Sembilan must also be respected,” he said.

items.title: Melaka heads for polls? CM Ab Rauf set to make big announcement today
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 22 — Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh is expected to announce the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly at 2pm today, paving the way for the 16th state election. Speculation over an imminent dissolution intensified after the state executive council meeting, usually held on Wednesdays, was brought forward by a day. In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats contested, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.

items.title: Passenger falls onto tracks at Wangsa Maju LRT station after reportedly fainting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — A passenger reportedly fainted before falling onto the tracks at the Wangsa Maju LRT station this morning, causing a brief disruption to services on the Kelana Jaya line. Rapid KL said the incident occurred at 6.52am. The passenger was rescued from the track area by station personnel and taken to the emergency department for immediate treatment, Rapid KL said.

items.title: Bukit Aman: Eight minors, two civil servants among 53 arrested over child sexual abuse materials
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Eight minors aged between 13 and 18 were among dozens arrested for possessing child child sexual abuse materials (CSAM) in a joint operation by Bukit Aman’s Criminal Investigation Department and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar told a press conference here that the minors were being investigated for possessing and selling animated CSAM made using artificial intelligence (AI), describing it as a “worrying trend”. “What is most worrying about this is that among those arrested were minors and civil servants,” he said today.

items.title: Miti says Bumiputera equity policy is not under its purview but Economy Ministry’s
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) today clarified that it has no information regarding matters related to the Bumiputera equity ownership policy. Miti said the matter falls under the purview of the Ministry of Economy. The statement was issued following a media statement by the Ministry of Education on Sept 21 regarding the standardisation of ownership requirements for private educational institutions under the ministry.

items.title: Leatherback makes third Terengganu landing this month, lays 70 eggs
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 22 — The Department of Fisheries Malaysia (DOF), through the Rantau Abang Turtle and Marine Ecosystem Centre (TCIC), recorded three leatherback turtle (Dermochelys coriacea) landings along the Terengganu coast this month, involving 195 eggs that were transferred to a controlled incubation site for protection. Director-General of Fisheries Datuk Adnan Hussain said the records provide important data to monitor leatherback turtle landings, protect the eggs and improve their survival chances. The first nesting was recorded at Pasir Putih Beach, Marang, on Sept 1, involving 44 eggs, followed by 81 eggs at Rantau Abang Beach on Sept 13 and 70 eggs at Kuala Abang Beach today.

items.title: Kelantan investment manager loses RM1.2m in savings and jewellery after scammers spoof police phone number
items.summary: Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the woman, a single mother in her 50s, received a call from an individual posing as an authority and claiming that she was involved in a money laundering case. Mohd Yusoff said the syndicate also used application spoofing technology to make the phone number appear as though the call was from the police, including using the Kelantan IPK’s telephone number. He said police detected about 68 calls a day using the Kelantan IPK’s number, and the matter was now under investigation.

items.title: Penang wants more than tourist numbers as it shifts to high-value tourism
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 22 — Penang is seeking the federal government’s support through Budget 2027 to strengthen its tourism agenda, including improving air connectivity, attracting more international events and preserving George Town’s heritage. State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the priorities were aimed at increasing the value of the tourism sector while ensuring its growth continued to benefit the local economy and community. Wong said Penang was also seeking a larger federal matching fund to bid for and attract international conferences, exhibitions, sporting events, festivals, concerts, as well as large-scale arts and cultural events.

items.title: Uncle remanded seven days over death of five-year-old girl allegedly thrown into Johor river
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 22 — A 37-year-old man who allegedly threw his five-year-old niece into a river in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili here, causing her death yesterday, has been remanded for seven days to assist in the investigation. It was reported yesterday that police arrested a local man for allegedly throwing his niece into a river, resulting in her death. Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said police received a report at about 9.30am before arresting the suspect.

items.title: Beyond minimum wage, Malaysia needs clearer wage ladders tied to productivity, says Akmal Nasrullah
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 22 — Wage compression is hindering working Malaysians from receiving proper compensation despite the narrowing wage gap between low- and semi-skilled workers in Malaysia, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today. Citing a recent Bank Negara report, Akmal Nasrullah said the wage difference between low- and semi-skilled workers had narrowed from RM550 in 2016 to RM396 in 2024. As such, he said raising the floor wage was only a starting point and the ministry must develop clearer wage ladders that keep pace with productivity.

items.title: Penang’s Chung Ling high school classroom catches fire, no casualties but 20pc damaged
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 22 — A classroom at SMK(C) Chung Ling in Ayer Itam here caught fire last night, with no casualties reported. The Penang Fire and Rescue Department said 12 personnel and three fire engines from the Paya Terubong and Lebuh Pantai fire and rescue stations were sent to the school after an emergency call was received at 7.54pm. He said there were no school activities taking place when the fire broke out and no casualties were reported.

items.title: Kelantan commercial crime losses hit RM33.5m in first eight months of 2026 as scam surge
items.summary: Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the number of commercial crime cases also rose from 1,100 to 1,921, an increase of 821 cases. However, Mohd Yusoff said the overall crime index for the Kelantan contingent from January to August this year fell three per cent to 1,213 cases compared with 1,251 cases during the same period in 2025. He said violent crime also declined 11 per cent from 310 to 276 cases, while property crime fell from 941 to 937 cases.

items.title: Bukit Aman denies police MPV escorted cable theft vehicle in Ampang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Police have denied claims circulating online that a Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) escorted a vehicle believed to be carrying stolen cables in Kampung Tasik Tambahan, Ampang, last Saturday. Sinar Harian reported that Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said police had arrested a cable theft suspect in connection with the incident. He said claims that the police vehicle was involved in a conspiracy with the cable thieves were untrue.

items.title: Education Ministry opens private schools sector to all investors, no more 30pc Bumi rule
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 22 — A minimum of 30 per cent Bumiputera equity ownership is no longer a requirement for private limited companies operating private educational institutions (IPS) under the Ministry of Education (MOE). The ministry said the decision was reached following discussions with the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry. The ministry noted the concerns raised regarding the 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement for specific IPS owned by private limited companies, as outlined in the IPS Policy Statement Book published in 2006.

items.title: Orang Asli man killed in suspected tiger attack while searching for rotan in Sungai Siput
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — An Orang Asli man was killed after he was believed to have been attacked by a tiger while searching for rotan in a forest area near Kampung Takung, Pos Perwor in Sungai Siput yesterday. Sinar Harian reported that Zamberi Angah, 42, was found dead in a bamboo clump near a logging road, about 200 metres from where the attack was believed to have taken place. The Malay daily reported that Zamberi was found at about 6.58pm in a bamboo clump near the logging road.

items.title: Maritime industry expert seeks Customs dept ruling on RM220m K8 cargoes, calls for industry-wide SOP on petroleum blending
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) has been urged to issue a clear written position on the Customs treatment of two petroleum cargoes with a combined declared value exceeding RM220 million, as continued uncertainty could affect shipping agents, terminal operators, cargo owners and other participants in Malaysia’s downstream petroleum sector. Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said the company was not asking JKDM to decide the matter in its favour, but to state the applicable law, procedure and documentary requirements in writing. The matter concerns two Atlanta Crude Oil cargoes totalling 76,954.325 metric tonnes.

items.title: Malaysia taps Gulf air links to grow Middle East tourism
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Malaysia is strengthening air connectivity and tourism cooperation with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and the wider Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region to boost tourist arrivals from the Middle East. According to Tourism Malaysia’s statement today, among the key outcomes were the signing of Memorandums of Understanding between Tourism Malaysia with Emirates and Qatar Airways to strengthen tourism promotion and joint marketing efforts. Also present was Tourism Malaysia director-general Mohd Amirul Rizal Abdul Rahim.

items.title: If inflation is falling, why do Malaysians still feel food prices biting hard?
items.summary: Inflation measures how quickly the overall prices of goods and services are rising, rather than whether prices themselves are high or low. When inflation falls, prices can continue to increase — only at a slower pace. The nasi lemak still costs RM5.61, even though inflation has fallen from 10 per cent to 2 per cent.

items.title: ‘This is where we were born’: 9,000 Kampung Bahagia residents wait to rebuild five months after devastating fire
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Sept 22 — Where a thousand wooden stilt houses once rose above the water, only blackened ruins remain. The floating village of Kampung Bahagia here was destroyed by a massive fire on April 19, leaving nearly 9,000 residents with nothing but the clothes on their backs. — Bernama pic Glimmer of hope Rohaida’s family is among the 100 or so families who have been living in the tents since the tragedy, without electricity or a regular supply of clean water.
